messages:
anya: quick follow-up on the adaptive-degrade idea from the RFC — noticed a couple corner cases when a tenant fires lots of low-quality short prompts rapidly. thinking about combining short-term scoring + token-budget windowing. TL;DR: propose a soft-degrade band that reduces model size and enforces a per-minute token cap per session.
kevin: can you paste the scoring heuristic? also how does this interact with Dedicated reserved capacity?
morgan: short answer: scoring = abuse_score = weighted(rls_rate, perplexity_est, duplicate_rate). threshold ~0.7 triggers soft-degrade. example: 
```
abuse_score = 0.6*rate_norm + 0.3*perplexity_norm + 0.1*dup_frac
```
leo: worried about false positives on eval traffic — many legitimate long-form explainers will look like high perplexity.
anya: agree. plan: require two-window confirmation (10s fast window, 2m confirmation) + model fallback to smaller family (redwood-1 -> redwood-1-small) rather than outright block.
kevin: how about customers on Dedicated? they may want opt-out or an explicit policy.
morgan: Dedicated customers can set policy to 'no automatic degrade' but we need guardrails: manual oversight + a "grace token" allowance. telemetry must expose 'degrade_event' per-tenant and reason.
ops-bot: deploy plan created: rls-degrade-v1 to staging at 1721002000.
leo: requests for metrics: add 'post_degrade_quality', 'degrades_per_hour', and a spike watch for eval_perplexity.
anya: checklist I added: 1) telemetry queries & panels, 2) config flags per-tenant, 3) rollback playbook, 4) test harness with synthetic spam profile. assigning @kevin playbook, @morgan telemetry, @leo tests.
kevin: playbook draft: include steps to lift degrade, manual override endpoint, audit log entries, and a customer notification template.
morgan: sample telemetry query for Grafana/Influx: 
```
SELECT mean(abuse_score) FROM tokens WHERE tenant='T123' AND time > now()-5m GROUP BY time(30s)
```
leo: small nit: normalize token rates by client qps to avoid penalizing batched requests.
anya: good catch. final architecture question: implement the decision in a sidecar or at the ingress/routing layer? sidecar = per-instance fast decisions, routing = global view.
kevin: prefer hybrid: sidecar for immediate enforcement (low latency), central confirmation service for cross-instance de-dup and policy store. sidecar will emit events, central will reconcile windows and escalate to hard block if confirmed.
morgan: propose minimal policy schema to start: 
```
policy: {degrade: auto|manual, grace_tokens: int, thresholds: {score_window_short_sec: int, score_window_long_sec: int}}
```
leo: approve :+1: 
anya: next steps: I'll write a short RFC follow-up with the schema, example configs, and telemetry panels. timeline: staging next week, prod gated by a two-week canary and QA.
ops-bot: canary rollout scheduled: start=1721004000 end=1721004600.
kevin: thanks all :eyes:
